about.title: Garden Grove Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Garden Grove sits at a busy crossroads of Orange County, and the numbers reflect that. In 2025, the city recorded 623 injury collisions, with 788 people hurt and 9 lives lost. A large share of those reports came from a handful of corridors: Garden Grove Boulevard, SR-22, Chapman Avenue, and Brookhurst Street. Friday evenings, roughly 5 to 7 p.m., tend to be when the reports cluster. If one of those collisions involved you, the days that follow can feel disorganized. Insurance adjusters call quickly. Medical bills arrive before you know the full extent of your injuries. Meanwhile, California gives you two years to file a claim in most cases, and only six months to give notice if a city or state agency is involved. LawProactive exists to make one part of this simpler. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that matches you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims in Garden Grove and works on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case recovers money.

whyChoose.title: Why Garden Grove Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you share some blame for a crash on Brookhurst Street or Chapman Avenue. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of responsibility.

items.title: Deadlines Are Tracked From Day One
items.desc: Most California car accident claims must be filed within two years, but claims involving Caltrans, the city, or another public agency can require notice in as little as six months. The attorneys we connect you with know which clock applies.

items.title: Evidence Is Protected Before It Disappears
items.desc: Dashcam footage, witness contact information, and vehicle damage photos fade fast. An independent attorney can move to preserve them, and can advise you not to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement before you have counsel.

items.question: I was hit on SR-22 near Garden Grove. Does that change my deadline?
items.answer: It might. If a road condition, signal, or public vehicle contributed to the crash, a government entity such as Caltrans or the city could be involved, and California typically requires a formal claim within six months rather than two years. That is one reason it helps to speak with an attorney early rather than waiting to see how the insurance process unfolds.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are generally not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and doing so before speaking with an attorney can hurt your claim. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that minimize what their company pays. It is reasonable to politely decline until you have had a chance to get advice.

items.question: How much does it cost to use LawProactive and hire an attorney?
items.answer: LawProactive is completely free. The independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, which means they are paid a percentage of any recovery rather than charging you up front. If your case does not result in a recovery, you owe no attorney fee.
